newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Tuesday on a lack of market-moving news, traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 3,348 yuan ($404) per tonne, losing 33 yuan. It opened at 3,380 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,390 and a low of 3,346.
July fell 47 to 3,295, September rose five to 3,386, the January 1998 contract gained two yuan to 3,382 and March rose five yuan to 3,385 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 15,000 tonnes from 16,200 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mixed and moved around opening levels for most of the session, traders said.
"The active stock markets are attracting investors away from the soybean market and only some speculators trading soybean contracts for quick profits," one trader said.
"There's a total lack of market-moving news and this is what is keeping soybean prices in their narrow range," he said.
Traders said they expected soybean prices would move little over the next few days.
